MIT makes undergraduate admission decisions for the Institute as a whole, not by major or department.

facts.value: Imperial assesses Home/Overseas status after application under UK regulations. A questionnaire is requested only when needed. Settled status and ordinary residence, generally three years before the first academic year, have exceptions; nationality alone is insufficient. September courses use 1 September as the first academic-year date. ELQ status is separately assessed, with STEM and some healthcare exemptions; affected higher charges are stated with an offer. Appeal before enrolment within one calendar month of initial assessment; status cannot be amended after starting.

facts.value: For 2026/27, eligible first-year undergraduates, Oxbridge medics and official full-year exchange students receive a bed-space guarantee only after firm Imperial conditional/unconditional acceptance, a housing application by 17 July 2026 and unconditional academic acceptance by 23 August 2026, while attending alone full-time for the full 26 September 2026–26 June 2027 year. A preferred hall is not guaranteed; preferences have equal rank. Insurance/clearing applicants, part-year exchange, non-exchange occasional study, intercalated BSc Medicine and Graduate Entry Medicine are excluded; the latter is undergraduate academically but treated as postgraduate for housing. Under-18 students must use a single room, not a twin, and provide parent/guardian consent. Postgraduate and Silwood rooms are not guaranteed. Utilities, internet, basic contents insurance, maintenance and communal cleaning remain included as stated by the original overview. Private-housing advice, contract checks and conditional guarantor support are separate resources. The 2027/28 cutoffs and terms remain unverified.

facts.value: Postgraduate taught: Applicants may be considered with either a five-year Specialist Diploma or a four-year Bachelor’s degree. Both routes require an overall average of at least 4.5/5, or 3.6/4 on a four-point scale. Doctoral study: Applicants should hold a Master’s degree with at least 4/5; 4.5/5 is normally preferred. Institutional recognition does not replace higher course-specific grades, relevant-field requirements, or other qualifications, and does not guarantee admission.

facts.value: Applicants must satisfy every condition in their offer before registration. Imperial verifies academic qualifications through the specific Qualification Check link in the offer; applicants should use that link rather than opening the platform separately. English test results are verified online using the appropriate test reference or referral. Email results for other accepted English qualifications to the Admissions team. If the offer requires ATAS, obtain the certificate before applying for a visa; it is valid for six months. The offer-holder page still lists IELTS Indicator verification instructions, but this historical verification list does not add IELTS Indicator to the current accepted-test list.

facts.value: For academic year 2026–27, self-paying undergraduate and postgraduate students with Unconditional Firm status may request payment in two instalments if they have no overdue balance and their course lasts at least eight months. Fully sponsored students are ineligible. Requests go through ASK Student Hub Online. Undergraduate and September-start postgraduate fees are due 50% on 1 August 2026 and 50% on 4 January 2027. October-start postgraduate fees are due 50% on 1 September 2026 and 50% on 4 January 2027. January-start postgraduate fees are due 50% on 4 January 2027 and 50% on 1 April 2027. Postgraduate research students pay 50% by the start of study and 50% in programme month four. Students who need a visa may use instalments but must still show evidence of funds for tuition and living costs.

facts.value: Until a sponsoring organisation’s award is formally confirmed and accepted by Imperial, tuition fees remain the applicant’s responsibility. Any amount not covered by an accepted sponsorship must be paid by the applicable deadline. Scholarship money paid directly to an individual is not formal sponsorship to Imperial; personal sponsors are also not treated as formal sponsors. Applicants awaiting sponsorship should declare self-funding until Imperial confirms it. Fully sponsored students cannot enrol until proof is accepted; partially sponsored students declare self-funding and may use the self-funding instalment terms. Evidence is usually an original, dated, authorised letter on headed paper giving the student name and CID, course, covered fee amount, invoice address, any purchase-order number, and confirmation of direct payment to Imperial.

facts.value: If an undergraduate withdraws or interrupts during a session, tuition is charged pro rata by each week or part-week studied, normally using a 31-week academic session (longer courses may use a longer session). Postgraduate withdrawal/interruption and postgraduate research writing-up charges use each week or part-week in a 52-week session. Any excess payment is refunded; on interruption it may instead be held for the student’s return. Sponsor-funded fees are charged/refunded on the same pro-rata basis. Tuition refunds are separate from postgraduate deposit refunds. Application fees become non-refundable after the initial 14-day cancellation period.

facts.value: Applicants applying for a UK student visa from overseas, or in the UK without at least 12 months’ permission, must show funds for one academic year of tuition (up to nine months) and up to nine months of UKVI maintenance. Unless relying on an official loan or sponsorship, funds must be held for 28 consecutive days, with the period ending within 31 days of the visa application. Exempt nationalities may not need to submit evidence but still need sufficient funds. Imperial does not require an advance tuition payment to issue a CAS, and payment does not guarantee a visa. A CAS requires an accepted unconditional offer and passport details uploaded to My Imperial. Payments can take up to five working days to process; a CAS update after receipt takes about 3–5 working days. Sponsor payments are not uploaded to the CAS; provide UKVI with an official sponsor letter.

facts.value: The three-week pre-sessional is a full-time, in-person orientation course for prospective undergraduate and postgraduate students who have already met the English requirement for their Imperial degree and hold an unconditional degree offer by the course start. It does not waive the degree’s English requirement. Imperial Business School applicants are excluded. The 2026 course ran 1–18 September at South Kensington and cost £2,580; applications are closed. Applications for 2027 courses are due to open in March 2027, but dates and prices were not yet published in the checked source. Applicants who do not meet the three-week eligibility rules may be eligible for the distinct six-week course. Places depend on capacity. Offers usually need acceptance within 28 days and at least five weeks before the start; fees are normally due in full within 14 days of invoice, unless the start date is close. Applicants must meet all conditions, including visa and enrolment requirements, by the course start.

facts.value: Imperial undergraduate degree courses are full-time; the university does not currently offer part-time or online-only undergraduate degrees. Applicants may apply using predicted school grades, but final results are required only after an offer is made and accepted. Transfer applications are accepted by Life Sciences, Mathematics, and Physics; Faculty of Engineering departments do not accept transfers. facts.value: For 2027–28 entry, undergraduate applications use UCAS, Imperial institution code I50. UCAS charges £34.50 per application regardless of the number of choices. facts.value: For undergraduate applicants to 2027–28 entry, contextual consideration requires Home fee status or an appropriate UK residential status plus at least one listed criterion: care experience; a permanent home postcode in England’s IMD quintile 1; current or recent free-school-meal eligibility within the last six years; or a permanent postcode in POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2 plus first-generation higher-education status, attendance at an English school below Imperial’s key-stage-5 performance threshold (20th percentile), or attendance at a school in the UK with free-school-meal rate above Imperial’s 80th-percentile threshold. The permanent home address counts, not the school address. Assessment uses UCAS information available by the applicable deadline; later changes are not considered. Other medical, personal, or family circumstances are not this scheme’s eligibility criteria and should be reported through the referee and, where relevant, the test provider. Contextual status may provide a guaranteed interview only when Imperial flags the application, predicted grades meet AAA or equivalent, and any applicable departmental contextual test threshold is met. A guaranteed minimum offer has its own AAA, motivation, and department test/interview criteria; Medical Biosciences additionally requires first-sitting qualifications for a guaranteed offer, though resit applicants may still receive holistic contextual consideration. Reconsideration is limited to eligible applicants notified in their rejection letter, for the same course, who achieved that course’s minimum and completed required test/interview, and only where places remain. The 2027 reconsideration form is scheduled for 12 August 2027 from 09:00 to 13:00 UK time; the applicant needs their UCAS Personal ID. The page labels one section “2026 entry support” while publishing the criteria and dates for 2027 entry, so preserve this source conflict.

fee_status: Overseas

facts.value: For 2027–28, Imperial expects to award at least 300 competitive Imperial Inspires scholarships to full-time Overseas-fee-paying undergraduate and selected postgraduate taught students. Eligibility is limited to courses/departments confirmed through the course or scholarship search; it does not cover every course. Each award is at least £15,000 per year for the full course duration, excluding repeat years and pausing during interruption. The faculty decides the tuition/maintenance split, stated in the award letter. Eligible applicants who meet the course minimums are invited to submit a separate application through i360 after applying for admission; scholarship assessment does not change the admission decision. Undergraduate awards are due by mid-April 2027; postgraduate taught outcomes follow the relevant admissions-round decision. Admission and award conditions must be met before registration. The scholarship requires satisfactory academic progression and annual review when it lasts more than 11 months; donor thank-you/update activities may be required and travel may not be reimbursed. Awards cannot be deferred: a deferred applicant must reapply in the new cycle. A student cannot hold this alongside a full tuition-and-maintenance scholarship or exceed the London maintenance cap; multiple partial awards are considered case by case and must be reported. A fee-status change ends eligibility. Non-registration or withdrawal stops payments; interruption pauses them and repeat years postpone them. Tuition is paid to Imperial and maintenance to a UK bank account on My Imperial. Students need funds for initial expenses while opening that account. Payments are normally made on the seventh of each month, with bank details required by midnight on the 20th of the previous month; initial payment requires registration. Imperial may recover overpayments or withdraw an award for breach. The dedicated 2027 application guidance now publishes course-class exclusions and separate undergraduate and postgraduate processes. Undergraduate applicants have an optional 250-word statement and a 5 February 2027 scholarship deadline; postgraduate applicants have no additional written task and two weeks from invitation. The department dates are admissions cutoffs for scholarship consideration, not universal scholarship-form deadlines. Selected Medicine and Natural Sciences courses still require course participation and an invitation; the joint RCA application must not inherit My Imperial scholarship participation.

country_and_region_panels.published_text: Applicants may be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA, etc, on a case by case basis provided that they have graduated with an overall mark of at least 8.5/10.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA, etc, applicants should have completed a Diplome d'Etat, Diplome d'Ingenieur or Ingenieur d'Etat with a final overall mark of at least 16/20.
Doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should also hold a Magister degree, normally with at least 16/20.

Postgraduate taught study
Applicants may be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MPH, MEd, MBA, etc, on a case by case basis provided that they have graduated with a Bàtxelor with a minimum grade of 7/10. Usually, a grade of 8/10 is preferred.
Doctoral study
Applicants may be considered for admission to a postgraduate doctoral course if they hold:
a Bàtxelor degree; and
a Master's degree with grades specified above.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA etc, applicants should have completed a Grau de Mestre with a minimum grade of 15/20 or better.
Doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should seek advice from the relevant Admissions team.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA etc, applicants should have:
completed a minimum of 4 years of study; and
been awarded the Licenciado with an overall grade of at least 7.5/10 from a mainstream university.
Doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should also hold a Magister degree with at least 7.5/10 from a mainstream university.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA etc, applicants should have:
completed a minimum of 4 years of study; and
been awarded the Bakalavr with an overall average grade of 4.5/5 or better.
Doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should hold a Master's degree with a grade of 4/5 or better, although a grade of 4.5/5 is normally preferred.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA, etc, applicants should hold a Bachelor's degree, to Honours level, with a minimum of a Lower Second Class Honours.
A minimum of an Upper Second Class honours is however normally required for most of our courses.
Postgraduate doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should hold:
a first degree, ideally with Honours; and
a Master's degree.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA, etc, applicants who graduated before the Bologna reforms should hold a Diploma with a grade of 2 or better.
Applicants who graduated after the Bologna reforms should hold a 1st cycle Bachelor's degree of at least 3 years' duration with a grade of 2 or better.
Postgraduate doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should be in possession of a 2nd cycle Master's degree normally with an overall grade of 2 or better.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA etc, applicants should have:
completed five years of study and been awarded the Specialist Diploma; or
completed four years of study and been awarded the Bachelor’s degree.
For both qualifications the requirement is an overall average grade of 4.5/5 or better.
Postgraduate doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should hold a Master's degree with a grade of 4/5 or better, although a grade of 4.5/5 is normally preferred.

University of Bharain
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA etc, applicants should hold a Bachelor's degree from the University of Bahrain with a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or better.
Postgraduate doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should also hold a Master's degree with a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or better.
Arabian Gulf University
Applicants from the Arabian Gulf University should hold a Bachelor’s degree awarded with 75% or better.
Postgraduate doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should hold a Master’s degree with Very Good or better.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA etc, applicants from the Bangladesh University of Engineering Technology should have completed a minimum of 4 years of study and have been awarded a Bachelor's degree with 75%.
Postgraduate doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should also hold a Master's degree with First Class or better.

To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA, etc, applicants should hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum of a Lower Second Class Honours from one of the campuses of the University of the West Indies.
A minimum of an Upper Second Class Honours is however normally required for most of our courses.
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should hold a first degree with a First or Upper Second Class Honours and should also be in possession of a Master's degree.

To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA etc, applicants should have completed a minimum of 5 years of study and been awarded a specialist degree or a Bachelor's degree with an overall average grade of 4.5/5 or better.
Where a 10-point grading scheme is used, 9/10 or better is required.

To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA, etc, applicants should hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum of Lower Second Class Honours from one of the campuses of the University of the West Indies.
A minimum of Upper Second Class honours is however normally required for most of our courses.
Doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should hold:
a first degree with First or Upper Second Class Honours; and
a Master's degree with 65% or better.

To be considered for admission to postgraduate study, applicants should have completed a Bachelor's and Master's degree with ‘Very Good' or better.
Departments seek applicants achieving 80% or better overall.
To be considered for admission to postgraduate study, applicants should hold a Bachelor and Master's degree from a mainstream university, achieved with 65% or better.

Postgraduate taught study
To be considered for admission to a Master's e.g. MSc, MRes, MBA, etc, applicants should hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum of Lower Second Class Honours from a mainstream university.
A minimum of Upper Second Class honours is however normally required for most of our courses.
Doctoral study
Applicants for a postgraduate doctoral course should hold:
a first degree with First or Upper Second Class Honours; and
a Master's degree with 65% or better.

value.academic: Award requirements are separate from PhD admission: a first-class/equivalent undergraduate or integrated master, or standalone-master distinction. Failure can revoke funding despite admission; final award confirmation requires both sets of conditions.
value.route_start: For a President PhD award holder on a 1+3 MRes/MSc then PhD route, the award starts at the PhD stage after MRes/MSc distinction; the initial master's fees and maintenance require separate funding. For a President PhD award holder undertaking a Research Council-funded CDT, that President scholarship starts at CDT entry for 3.5 years only, leaving the final six months' costs to the student and department. This does not shorten a separate four-year HealthBRIDGE or other CDT grant.
value.consumables: GBP2,000 annually for the first three years is paid into the supervisor account for direct PhD expenses including conference travel and specialist resources, not standard-specification laptops or laboratory enhancement. Unspent balances carry forward; a final-year balance must be spent or returned within six months.
value.continuation: Satisfactory academic progress is required, with annual eligibility review for awards longer than 11 months. Donor updates/events may be required; travel is not necessarily reimbursed. A paid full-time internship may suspend the stipend, which resumes preserving the full 3.5-year entitlement.
value.research_students: Writing-up funding may continue for up to12 months only while solely writing the thesis and subject to the award letter. Full-time employment is ineligible; part-time employment may qualify for a half award. Contractual Imperial employees cannot receive stipends except casual contracts subject to Student Financial Support advice.
value.payment_and_changes: Registration and UK bank details are needed; monthly payment is normally on the7th, with the20th of the prior month as cutoff. Initial personal funds are needed before payments start. Notify other awards and overpayments. Full awards cannot be stacked; partial combinations are assessed case by case with a2026/27 research maintenance cap ofGBP26,500. Interruption or repeat may postpone or stop funding; withdrawal stops it and excess payments are recoverable. Awards are non-transferable and cannot be deferred: reapply in the next cycle. Named Parental Leave, Support Fund and UROP exceptions remain award-specific.

Martingale Scholarships: Full details and how to apply Overseas fee Overseas fee - Applied + Pure + Pure Formalisation Full-time £44,800 total fee Part-time £22,400 per year Inflationary increases You should expect and budget for your fees to increase each year. Your fee is based on the year you enter the university, not your year of study. This means that if you repeat a year or resume your studies after an interruption, your fees will only increase by the amount linked to inflation. Find out more about our tuition fees payment terms , including how inflationary increases are applied to your tuition fees in subsequent years of study. Which fee you pay Whether you pay the Home or Overseas fee depends on your fee status. This is assessed based on UK Government legislation and includes things like where you live and your nationality or residency status. Find out how we assess your fee status . Postgraduate Master's Loan If you're a UK national, or EU national with settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, you may be able to apply for a Postgraduate Master’s Loan from the UK government, if you meet certain criteria. The maximum value of the loan is £13,206 if your course starts on or after 1 August 2026. The loan is not means-tested and you can choose whether to put it towards your tuition fees or living costs. Please note that the loan is only available if you’re studying a full Master’s course from the start. If you start on a Postgraduate Certificate (PG Cert) or Postgraduate Diploma (PG Dip) and later move on to the Master’s, you won’t be eligible for this loan. Martingale Scholarships: Full details and how to apply Overseas fee Overseas fee - Applied + Pure + Pure Formalisation Full-time £44,800 total fee Part-time £22,400 per year Inflationary increases You should expect and budget for your fees to increase each year. Your fee is based on the year you enter the university, not your year of study. This means that if you repeat a year or resume your studies after an interruption, your fees will only increase by the amount linked to inflation. Find out more about our tuition fees payment terms , including how inflationary increases are applied to your tuition fees in subsequent years of study. Which fee you pay Whether you pay the Home or Overseas fee depends on your fee status. This is assessed based on UK Government legislation and includes things like where you live and your nationality or residency status. Find out how we assess your fee status . Postgraduate Master's Loan If you're a UK national, or EU national with settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, you may be able to apply for a Postgraduate Master’s Loan from the UK government, if you meet certain criteria. The maximum value of the loan is £13,206 if your course starts on or after 1 August 2026. The loan is not means-tested and you can choose whether to put it towards your tuition fees or living costs. Please note that the loan is only available if you’re studying a full Master’s course from the start. If you start on a Postgraduate Certificate (PG Cert) or Postgraduate Diploma (PG Dip) and later move on to the Master’s, you won’t be eligible for this loan. Learn more about the Postgraduate Master's Loan . Martingale Scholarships The Martingale Foundation are offering fully funded scholarships for eligible students on selected Mathematics courses. Martingale Scholarships: Full details and how to apply Scholarships View all scholarships Martingale Scholarships Value per award Varies Who it's for All applicants to Mathematics postgraduate courses. Find out more Structure This page is updated regularly to reflect the latest version of the curriculum. However, this information is subject to change. Find out more about potential course changes . Please note: it may not always be possible to take specific combinations of modules due to timetabling conflicts. For confirmation, please check with the relevant department. Optional modules Research project Optional modules You'll choose eight modules that account for two-thirds of your overall grade. Part-time students will choose four modules in the first year and four in the second year. There are no mandatory core modules except the research project. Taught modules Probability Theory 1 Explore the fundamental properties of probability, including probability measures. independent random variables and elements of Brownian motion. Functional Analysis Assess ideas of continuity and linear algebra, with a particular emphasis on vector spaces and linear maps. Fourier Analysis and Theory of Distributions Deepen your understanding of Fourier analysis and how the Fourier transform works. Stochastic Calculus with Applications to Non-Linear Filtering Become familiar with the stochastic calculus in relation to non-linear filtering and modern numerical methods for solving the filtering problem. Probability Theory 2 Discover why Markov processes are widely used to model random evolutions and how the theory connects with many other subjects in mathematics. Geometry of Curves and Surfaces Understand the curvature of a surface in 3-dimensional space and expand your knowledge of topological surfaces. Algebraic Curves Build your understanding of algebraic curves and explore concepts including Meromorphic differentials and Abel's theorem. Algebraic Topology Engage with algebraic topology and advance your knowledge of homology theory, fundamental groups and the Galois correspondence for covering spaces. Algebraic Geometry Learn to use algebraic and geometric ideas together, studying basic concepts from both perspectives and applying them to numerous examples. Riemannian Geometry Appreciate geodesics and curvature and the relationship between them and use these ideas to analyse how local geometric conditions can lead to global topological constraints. Manifolds Explore the foundations and examples of manifolds, including smooth manifolds, quotients, tangent spaces and vector bundles. Differential Topology Delve into key aspects of differential topology, which is concerned with the topology of smooth manifolds. Complex Manifolds Enhance your understanding of the theory of almost complex manifolds and complex manifolds, considering examples including Kähler manifolds and complex projective manifolds. Algebra 3 Further your appreciation of algebra and explore the basics of homological algebra, complexes and exact sequences. Group Theory Familiarise yourself with key concepts on this introduction to some of the more advanced topics in the theory of groups. Galois Theory Examine Galois theory and why the formula for the solution to a quadratic equation is well-known, while no formula is possible for quintics. Graph Theory Study the elementary theory of graphs and analyse why graphs are used in many areas of mathematics and other fields. Group Representation Theory Explore the representations of groups and the character of a group representation. Formalising Mathematics Discover how computer theorem provers are maturing and improve your understanding of this area of mathematics by studying the Lean theorem prover. Commutative Algebra Develop your knowledge further with this introduction to commutative algebra that looks into the prime and maximal ideals, the nilradical and the Jacobson radical. Lie Algebras Explore semisimple complex Lie algebras and the classification of irreducible representations. Algebra 4 Analyse a range of advanced algebra topics, incorporating aspects of number theory, geometry and topology. Number Theory Examine the properties of natural numbers and assess various theorems relating to number theory. Algebraic Number Theory Gain an appreciation for algebraic number theory and advance your understanding of quadratic fields. Elliptic Curves Explore the different types of elliptic curves and investigate the Mordell-Weil theorem. Advanced Partial Differential Equations 1 Develop an understanding of partial differential equations (PDE) appearing in physics and geometry, and classical techniques to study them analytically. Mathematical Logic Analyse the way in which we reason formally about mathematical structures and look at the ZFC axioms to develop the notion of cardinality. Geometric Complex Analysis Analyse geometric notions associated with domains in the plane and their boundaries, and how they are transformed under holomorphic mappings. Theory of Partial Differential Equations Explore how partial differential equations can be used to model real-world phenomena, while developing the mathematical tools to analyse these models and gaining an introduction to numerical methods. Advanced Partial Differential Equations 1 Develop your understanding of partial differential equations and the analytical techniques used across scientific disciplines, with a focus on weak solutions, regularity, and the mathematical theory underpinning elliptic and parabolic equations. Advanced Partial Differential Equations 2 Explore the theory of nonlinear partial differential equations and develop modern analytical techniques, such as fixed-point theorems and Fourier analysis, to tackle problems in areas including fluid mechanics and wave propagation. Research project You'll also complete a research project based around a mathematical topic from the core course area. This could include elements of analysis, algebra, combinatorics, geometry and number theory. The project will be assessed by a written report and an oral examination.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) and interview Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Mathematics 2 Physics Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sitting windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1 : 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2 : 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1 : 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2 : 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK) . Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the ESAT , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare. Interview When are applicants invited for an interview? Applicants will be invited for an interview with our academic staff should they exhibit excellent cumulative performance throughout the admission stages. How long is the interview and what purpose does it serve? This interview lasts about 25 - 30 minutes. It serves as an opportunity for a two-way conversation between the interviewer and the applicant to ask questions and probe further. There are several elements that are being explored, including the applicant's motivations, academic ambitions and their suitability for our courses. When does it take place? Interviews will usually be scheduled after the ESAT test, and we aim to inform applicants of the confirmed schedule approximately 1 week in advance. Find out more about Aeronautics admissions.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) and interview Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Mathematics 2 Physics Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sitting windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1 : 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2 : 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1 : 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2 : 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK) . Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the ESAT , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare. Interview When are applicants invited for an interview? Applicants will be invited for an interview with our academic staff should they exhibit excellent cumulative performance throughout the admission stages. How long is the interview and what purpose does it serve? This interview lasts about 25 - 30 minutes. It serves as an opportunity for a two-way conversation between the interviewer and the applicant to ask questions and probe further. There are several elements that are being explored, including the applicant's motivations, academic ambitions and their suitability for our courses. When does it take place? Interviews will usually be scheduled after the ESAT test, and we aim to inform applicants of the confirmed schedule approximately 1 week in advance. Find out more about Aeronautics admissions.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Chemistry Biology Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sittings windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1: 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2: 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1: 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2: 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK). Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the ESAT , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Chemistry Biology Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sittings windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1: 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2: 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1: 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2: 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK). Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the ESAT , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Chemistry Biology Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sittings windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1: 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2: 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1: 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2: 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK). Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test and interview This department does not use a test as part of its selection process. Predicted grades and scores in your application are important, but it’s not the only thing that drives the decision. Our selectors will also consider things like your personal statement and your references to understand whether there is a good match between you and your chosen subject and department at Imperial. You can read more about our selection process, including tips on writing a personal statement, in our How to Apply section. Interview Post-application open day and interview If your UCAS application indicates that you are likely to satisfy our requirements, you will be invited to an applicant day. Applicant days are held on Wednesdays between November and March and run from 10.30 to 15.30. You will be expected to attend the whole day. During an applicant day, you will hear from our Director of Undergraduate Studies and then our Admission Tutor. Activities include: A 30 minute one-to-one interview with one of our lecturers. We aim for the interview to be more of a conversation. The main purpose of the interview is for us to see whether you are suitable for the course, as much as for you to decide if Imperial is the place for you. A 45 minute group task. The task will be an engineering-based problem-solving challenge to see your team working skills, as we deem this to be an important part of life at Imperial. A 45 minute Q&A with current student ambassadors where you will be able to ask them questions about the course and studying in London.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test and interview This department does not use a test as part of its selection process. Predicted grades and prior educational achievement in your application are important, but it’s not the only thing that drives the decision. Our selectors will also consider things like your personal statement and your references to understand whether there is a good match between you and your chosen subject and department at Imperial. You can read more about our selection process, including tips on writing a personal statement, in our How to Apply section. Interview Post-application open day and interview When assessing applications, we will consider your examination results (already gained and predicted), your motivation and understanding of biomedical engineering as a career, your potential for leadership and teamwork, your interests and the referee’s report. You may be invited to an online interview if your UCAS application indicates that you are likely to satisfy our entry requirements and you demonstrate interest and motivation to study this course. Foundation programmes Imperial does not offer its own Foundation Programme. However, the following are accepted for entry to this programme: UCL’s Undergraduate Preparatory Certificate for Science and Engineering (UPCSE), and Warwick’s International Foundation Programme (IFP) in Science & Engineering UCL UPCSE Students complete four modules across the year – two compulsory and two elective modules. Compulsory modules: Research and Academic Skills: Science and Society Academic English Elective modules: Biology Chemistry Mathematics Physics Minimum requirements The Department of Bioengineering minimum requirements are: 80% overall 80% Mathematics and Physics Warwick IFP Science and Engineering The Department of Bioengineering minimum requirements are: 80% overall 80% Mathematics and Physics To meet these requirements, you should choose from the following IFP pathways: Engineering

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Chemistry Biology Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sittings windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1: 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2: 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1: 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2: 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK). Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the ESAT , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Chemistry Biology Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sittings windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1: 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2: 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1: 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2: 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK). Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the ESAT , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) and interview Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Mathematics 2 Chemistry Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sittings windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1: 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2: 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1: 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2: 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK). Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the ESAT , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare. course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test and interview This department does not use a test as part of its selection process. Predicted grades and scores in your application are important, but it’s not the only thing that drives the decision. Our selectors will also consider things like your personal statement and your references to understand whether there is a good match between you and your chosen subject and department at Imperial. You can read more about our selection process, including tips on writing a personal statement, in our How to Apply section. Interview Post-application open day and interview If assessment of your UCAS application indicates that you are likely to satisfy our requirements, you will be shortlisted for an academic interview as part of our interview programme. There will be a pre-recorded talk by the admissions tutor made available online, about the department, the structure of the course and other opportunities available to enrich your experience with us. There will also be talks and presentations available by the accommodation and finance teams, and from Horizons about the great range of modules they offer. We are organising online Q&A sessions, where you will have the chance to talk to the admissions tutor and to current undergraduates, and you can see more about the department on the Chemistry and Virtual Tour websites. We will run interviews in the morning and afternoon (UK time) to accommodate students in different time-zones, and each applicant will be interviewed individually. The interview will comprise a discussion with an experienced academic who will be looking to assess an applicant’s motivation for studying chemistry and their potential for the future. Although the discussion may begin with topics mentioned in the UCAS personal statement, the conversations will likely expand to cover topics that the applicant may not be so familiar with. This enables the interviewer to observe how an applicant thinks and how they reason their way through a problem. The interviewers are highly experienced and are able to see through nerves, stress and silly mistakes so you should not worry about answering the questions. There are no trick questions, if an answer seems obvious, it might be just that. We then use the interview feedback in combination with the UCAS application, to decide whether we are able to make an offer, and what the conditions of the offer will be. We will be making offer decisions only after all interviews are complete. We will aim to contact all applicants directly by e-mail, by early March with a decision. You should be able to see this updated on UCAS Hub by the end of March.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test and interview This department does not use a test as part of its selection process. Predicted grades and scores in your application are important, but it’s not the only thing that drives the decision. Our selectors will also consider things like your personal statement and your references to understand whether there is a good match between you and your chosen subject and department at Imperial. You can read more about our selection process, including tips on writing a personal statement, in our How to Apply section. Interview Post-application open day and interview If assessment of your UCAS application indicates that you are likely to satisfy our requirements, you will be shortlisted for an academic interview as part of our interview programme. There will be a pre-recorded talk by the admissions tutor made available online, about the department, the structure of the course and other opportunities available to enrich your experience with us. There will also be talks and presentations available by the accommodation and finance teams, and from Horizons about the great range of modules they offer. We are organising online Q&A sessions, where you will have the chance to talk to the admissions tutor and to current undergraduates, and you can see more about the department on the Chemistry and Virtual Tour websites. We will run interviews in the morning and afternoon (UK time) to accommodate students in different time-zones, and each applicant will be interviewed individually. The interview will comprise a discussion with an experienced academic who will be looking to assess an applicant’s motivation for studying chemistry and their potential for the future. Although the discussion may begin with topics mentioned in the UCAS personal statement, the conversations will likely expand to cover topics that the applicant may not be so familiar with. This enables the interviewer to observe how an applicant thinks and how they reason their way through a problem. The interviewers are highly experienced and are able to see through nerves, stress and silly mistakes so you should not worry about answering the questions. There are no trick questions, if an answer seems obvious, it might be just that. We then use the interview feedback in combination with the UCAS application, to decide whether we are able to make an offer, and what the conditions of the offer will be. We will be making offer decisions only after all interviews are complete. We will aim to contact all applicants directly by e-mail, by early March with a decision. You should be able to see this updated on UCAS Hub by the end of March. Foundation programmes Imperial does not offer its own Foundation Programme. However, the following are accepted for entry to this programme: UCL’s Undergraduate Preparatory Certificate for Science and Engineering (UPCSE) Language requirement: For a course including a year abroad, you will also need an appropriate modern foreign language at CEFR A2+. UCL UPCSE Students complete four modules across the year – two compulsory and two elective modules. Compulsory modules: Research and Academic Skills: Science and Society Academic English Elective modules: Biology Chemistry Mathematics Physics Minimum requirements The Department of Chemistry minimum requirements are: 80% overall 80% Chemistry 80% Mathematics

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test and interview This department does not use a test as part of its selection process. Predicted grades and scores in your application are important, but it’s not the only thing that drives the decision. Our selectors will also consider things like your personal statement and your references to understand whether there is a good match between you and your chosen subject and department at Imperial. You can read more about our selection process, including tips on writing a personal statement, in our How to Apply section. Interview Post-application open day and interview If assessment of your UCAS application indicates that you are likely to satisfy our requirements, you will be shortlisted for an academic interview as part of our interview programme. There will be a pre-recorded talk by the admissions tutor made available online, about the department, the structure of the course and other opportunities available to enrich your experience with us. There will also be talks and presentations available by the accommodation and finance teams, and from Horizons about the great range of modules they offer. We are organising online Q&A sessions, where you will have the chance to talk to the admissions tutor and to current undergraduates, and you can see more about the department on the Chemistry and Virtual Tour websites. We will run interviews in the morning and afternoon (UK time) to accommodate students in different time-zones, and each applicant will be interviewed individually. The interview will comprise a discussion with an experienced academic who will be looking to assess an applicant’s motivation for studying chemistry and their potential for the future. Although the discussion may begin with topics mentioned in the UCAS personal statement, the conversations will likely expand to cover topics that the applicant may not be so familiar with. This enables the interviewer to observe how an applicant thinks and how they reason their way through a problem. The interviewers are highly experienced and are able to see through nerves, stress and silly mistakes so you should not worry about answering the questions. There are no trick questions, if an answer seems obvious, it might be just that. We then use the interview feedback in combination with the UCAS application, to decide whether we are able to make an offer, and what the conditions of the offer will be. We will be making offer decisions only after all interviews are complete. We will aim to contact all applicants directly by e-mail, by early March with a decision. You should be able to see this updated on UCAS Hub by the end of March.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test and interview This department does not use a test as part of its selection process. Predicted grades and scores in your application are important, but it’s not the only thing that drives the decision. Our selectors will also consider things like your personal statement and your references to understand whether there is a good match between you and your chosen subject and department at Imperial. You can read more about our selection process, including tips on writing a personal statement, in our How to Apply section. Interview Post-application open day and interview If assessment of your UCAS application indicates that you are likely to satisfy our requirements, you will be shortlisted for an academic interview as part of our interview programme. There will be a pre-recorded talk by the admissions tutor made available online, about the department, the structure of the course and other opportunities available to enrich your experience with us. There will also be talks and presentations available by the accommodation and finance teams, and from Horizons about the great range of modules they offer. We are organising online Q&A sessions, where you will have the chance to talk to the admissions tutor and to current undergraduates, and you can see more about the department on the Chemistry and Virtual Tour websites. We will run interviews in the morning and afternoon (UK time) to accommodate students in different time-zones, and each applicant will be interviewed individually. The interview will comprise a discussion with an experienced academic who will be looking to assess an applicant’s motivation for studying chemistry and their potential for the future. Although the discussion may begin with topics mentioned in the UCAS personal statement, the conversations will likely expand to cover topics that the applicant may not be so familiar with. This enables the interviewer to observe how an applicant thinks and how they reason their way through a problem. The interviewers are highly experienced and are able to see through nerves, stress and silly mistakes so you should not worry about answering the questions. There are no trick questions, if an answer seems obvious, it might be just that. We then use the interview feedback in combination with the UCAS application, to decide whether we are able to make an offer, and what the conditions of the offer will be. We will be making offer decisions only after all interviews are complete. We will aim to contact all applicants directly by e-mail, by early March with a decision. You should be able to see this updated on UCAS Hub by the end of March.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (ESAT) and next steps Admissions test (ESAT) You must sit the Engineering and Science Admissions Test (ESAT) as part of the application process for this course. The ESAT is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which is divided into a number of modules. ESAT modules To be eligible for selection for this course, you will need to sit three ESAT modules: Mathematics 1 Mathematics 2 Physics Each module is made up of 27 multiple-choice questions and lasts 40 minutes. Make a note of which modules you will need to sit for course(s) of interest as you will need this information when you book your test. Test dates There are two test sittings windows for the ESAT for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1: 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2: 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1: 12–13 October 2026 Test window 2: 6 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October ESAT test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to register and book The ESAT is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK). Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose ESAT, your test date, modules, and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the ESAT , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare. Next steps Insight sessions Applicants who have the potential to meet the minimum entry requirements are invited to an insight session. This is an online event which runs for around an hour and gives applicants the opportunity to find out more about the course itself, the academics who teach on the course and student life in the department of Civil & Environmental Engineering. Insight sessions will be held on Wednesday 4 November 2026 (for applications received by 15 October) and on Wednesday 27 January 2027 (for all other applications). Video submission Applicants who have the potential to meet the minimum entry requirements are invited to make an online video submission. We will ask you to respond to questions that explore your motivation, experiences and reasoning skills. Example questions are not available. When does it take place? The video submission requirements will be emailed on Thursday 12 November 2026 (for applications received by 15 October) and on Thursday 4 February 2027 (for all other applications). Applicants will have 48 hours to complete the video submission. The video submission takes around 15 minutes to complete. When will you find out the results? The results of the test and video submission will then be considered along with all the information on your UCAS form in order to make the decision on the application. Please note that it may take several months to make a decision on your application. This is because we accept applications right up until the UCAS deadline in January. We read and assess all applications very carefully, and we continue making decisions right up to the end of March. Accordingly, even if you have applied in October, you may not hear anything until the end of March. Foundation programmes Imperial does not offer its own Foundation Programme. However, the following are accepted for entry to this programme: UCL's Undergraduate Preparatory Certificate for Science and Engineering (UPCSE), and Warwick's International Foundation Programme (IFP) in Science & Engineering UCL UPCSE Minimum requirements The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering minimum requirements are: 80% overall 80% Mathematics and Physics Warwick IFP Science and Engineering Minimum requirements The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering minimum requirements are: 80% overall 80% Mathematics and Physics To meet these requirements, you should choose from the following IFP pathways: Engineering

Test dates There are two test sitting windows for the TMUA for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1 : 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2 : 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1 : 15 –1 6 October 2026 Test window 2 : 8 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October TMUA test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to book a test The TMUA is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK) . Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose TMUA , your test date and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (TMUA) and interview Admissions test (TMUA) You must sit the Test for Mathematics for University Admission (TMUA) as part of the application process for this course. The Mathematics Admissions Test (MAT) is no longer used by Imperial. About TMUA The TMUA is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which tests your mathematical thinking and reasoning skills. Test dates There are two test sitting windows for the TMUA for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1 : 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2 : 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1 : 15 –1 6 October 2026 Test window 2 : 8 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October TMUA test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to book a test The TMUA is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK) . Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose TMUA , your test date and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the TMUA , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare. course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test (TMUA) and interview Admissions test (TMUA) You must sit the Test for Mathematics for University Admission (TMUA) as part of the application process for this course. The Mathematics Admissions Test (MAT) is no longer used by Imperial. About TMUA The TMUA is a computer-based, multiple-choice test, which tests your mathematical thinking and reasoning skills. Test dates There are two test sitting windows for the TMUA for 2027 entry. Candidates in most countries can book a time slot on any day within the test windows, though please note that those taking the test in China, Hong Kong, or Macau can only do so on specific dates within each window. These are listed separately below. For candidates in all countries except China, Hong Kong and Macau Test window 1 : 12–16 October 2026 Test window 2 : 4–8 January 2027 For candidates sitting the test in China, Macau and Hong Kong Test window 1 : 15 –1 6 October 2026 Test window 2 : 8 January 2027 Booking windows (all candidates) Test window 1 Booking for the October TMUA test sitting is now closed Booking closes: 28 September 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) Test window 2 Booking opens: 26 October 2026 at 15.00 (UK time) Booking closes: 21 December 2026 at 18.00 (UK time) How to book a test The TMUA is managed by University Admissions Tests UK (UAT-UK) . Step 1: Register with UAT-UK Registration is now open for you to create your UAT-UK account (only once, even if you retake the test). Step 2: Book your test Bookings for the October 2026 test window open on 20 July 2026 at 15:00 (UK time). When booking opens, log in to your UAT-UK account, choose TMUA , your test date and a Pearson centre, then pay the fee. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. More information Find out more about the TMUA , including information on how to book, test fees, bursaries for UK candidates in financial need, access arrangements and how to prepare. It is your responsibility to book and sit your test within the testing window. course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test and interview This department does not use a test as part of its selection process. Predicted grades and scores in your application are important, but it’s not the only thing that drives the decision. Our selectors will also consider things like your personal statement and your references to understand whether there is a good match between you and your chosen subject and department at Imperial. You can read more about our selection process, including tips on writing a personal statement, in our How to Apply section. Interview Post-application open day and interview If your UCAS application indicates that you are likely to satisfy our requirements you will be invited to participate in an interview, which may be online. If coming to an interview on campus, you will be introduced to the Department, the staff, our courses, teaching facilities and methods and life at College by staff and our current students. You will then have an interview with a member of the academic staff. We will run online interviews in the morning and afternoon (UK time) to accommodate students in different time-zones, and each applicant will be interviewed individually. The interview will comprise a discussion with an experienced academic who will be looking to assess an applicant’s motivation for studying earth sciences and their potential for the future. Whether in person or online, the interview is a chance for us to get to know each other, and we consider all aspects of your application fully when deciding whether to make you an offer. We will also take the comments of the staff member who has interviewed you into account, particularly when we decide after A-levels whether to confirm a place should you marginally fail to meet the terms of your offer.

course_specific_test_blocks: Admissions test and interview This department does not use a test as part of its selection process. Predicted grades and scores in your application are important, but it’s not the only thing that drives the decision. Our selectors will also consider things like your personal statement and your references to understand whether there is a good match between you and your chosen subject and department at Imperial. You can read more about our selection process, including tips on writing a personal statement, in our How to Apply section. Interview Post-application open day and interview If your UCAS application indicates that you are likely to satisfy our requirements you will be invited to participate in an interview, which may be online. If coming to an interview on campus, you will be introduced to the Department, the staff, our courses, teaching facilities and methods and life at College by staff and our current students. You will then have an interview with a member of the academic staff. We will run online interviews in the morning and afternoon (UK time) to accommodate students in different time-zones, and each applicant will be interviewed individually. The interview will comprise a discussion with an experienced academic who will be looking to assess an applicant’s motivation for studying earth sciences and their potential for the future. Whether in person or online, the interview is a chance for us to get to know each other, and we consider all aspects of your application fully when deciding whether to make you an offer. We will also take the comments of the staff member who has interviewed you into account, particularly when we decide after A-levels whether to confirm a place should you marginally fail to meet the terms of your offer.
